arxiv-2210-11964.title: Spiral arms and the angular momentum gap in Milky Way Cepheids 2022 Spiral arms and the angular momentum gap in Milky Way Cepheids – A
arxiv-2210-11964.creator: Marcin Semczuk, Walter Dehnen, Ralph Schönrich, E. Athanassoula
arxiv-2210-11964.description: Abstract The angular-momentum distribution of classical Cepheids in the outer Milky Way disc is bi-modal with a gap at L gap = 2950 ​ km s -1 L_{\mathrm{gap}}=2950\,\mbox{km\,s${}^{-1}$} kpc, corresponding to R = 13 R=13\, kpc, while no similar feature has been found in the general population of disc stars.

arxiv-2211-12021.title: ViFi-Loc: Multi-modal Pedestrian Localization using GAN with Camera-Phone Correspondences
arxiv-2211-12021.creator: Hansi Liu, Kristin Dana, Marco Gruteser, Hongsheng Lu
arxiv-2211-12021.description: Abstract In Smart City and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) systems, acquiring pedestrians’ accurate locations is crucial to traffic safety. Current systems adopt cameras and wireless sensors to detect and estimate people’s locations via sensor fusion. Standard fusion algorithms, however, become inapplicable when multi-modal data is not associated.

arxiv-2305-01180.title: Deep Q-Learning-based Distribution Network Reconfiguration for Reliability Improvement
arxiv-2305-01180.creator: Mukesh Gautam, Student Member, IEEE, Narayan Bhusal, Student Member, IEEE
arxiv-2305-01180.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mukesh Gautam, Student Member, IEEE, Narayan Bhusal, Student Member, IEEE. Distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) has proved to be an economical and effective way to improve the reliability of distribution systems. As optimal network configuration depends on system operating states (e.g., loads at each node), existing analytical and population-based approaches need to repeat the entire analysis and computation to find the optimal network configuration with a change in system operating states.

arxiv-2306-14563.title: Multi-output Ensembles for Multi-step Forecasting
arxiv-2306-14563.creator: Vitor Cerqueira, Luis Torgo
arxiv-2306-14563.description: Abstract This paper studies the application of ensembles composed of multi-output models for multi-step ahead forecasting problems. Dynamic ensembles have been commonly used for forecasting. However, these are typically designed for one-step ahead tasks. On the other hand, the literature regarding the application of dynamic ensembles for multi-step ahead forecasting is scarce.

arxiv-2307-11420.title: OU-HET 1176 Quantum phase transition and absence of quadratic divergence in generalized quantum field theories
arxiv-2307-11420.creator: Hikaru Kawai, Kiyoharu Kawana, Kin-ya Oda, and Kei Yagyu
arxiv-2307-11420.description: Abstract In ordinary thermodynamics, around first-order phase transitions, the intensive parameters such as temperature and pressure are automatically fixed to the phase transition point when one controls the extensive parameters such as total volume and total energy. From the microscopic point of view, the extensive parameters are more fundamental than the intensive parameters.

arxiv-2309-10638.title: Partial triangulations of surfaces with girth constraints Thanks: MSC2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. 05C10, 52C25 August 9, 2026
arxiv-2309-10638.creator: Stephen C. Power
arxiv-2309-10638.description: Abstract . Barnette and Edelson have shown that there are finitely many minimal triangulations of a connected compact 2-manifold ℳ {\mathcal{M}} . Similar finiteness results are obtained for cellular partial triangulations that satisfy various girth inequality constraints for embedded cycles.

arxiv-2406-12540.title: Heritability of Kőnig’s Property from finite edge sets Thanks: The first-named author gratefully acknowledges support by the Swiss National Science Foundation [grant number 200021 192079].
arxiv-2406-12540.creator: Marc Kaufmann, Dominic van der Zypen
arxiv-2406-12540.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Marc Kaufmann, Dominic van der Zypen. A hypergraph H = ( V , E ) H=(V,E) is said to have Kőnig’s Property if there is a matching M ⊆ E M\subseteq E and S ⊆ V S\subseteq V such that | S ∩ e | = 1 |S\cap e|=1 for all e ∈ M e\in M , and S S is a vertex cover of H H .

arxiv-2503-10757.title: Coherent control through phonon anharmonicity
arxiv-2503-10757.creator: Gili Scharf 1, Tomer Hasharoni 1, Lara Donval 1, Leah Ben Gur 1, Alon Ron 1
arxiv-2503-10757.description: Abstract Anharmonic lattice vibrations play a key role in many physical phenomena. They govern the heat conductivity of solids, strongly affect the phonon spectra, play a prominent role in soft mode phase transitions, allow ultrafast engineering of material properties and more.

arxiv-2507-08583.title: Classical Fluid Analogies for Schrödinger-Newton Systems
arxiv-2507-08583.creator: Peter Coles ∗, Aoibhinn Gallagher
arxiv-2507-08583.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Peter Coles ∗, Aoibhinn Gallagher. The Schrödinger-Poisson formalism has found a number of applications in cosmology, particularly in describing the growth by gravitational instability of large-scale structure in a universe dominated by ultra-light scalar particles. Here we investigate the extent to which the behaviour of this and the more general case of a Schrödinger-Newton system, can be described in terms of classical fluid concepts such as viscosity and pressure.

arxiv-2602-19561.title: Dynamic Sensor Scheduling Based on Node Partitioning of Graphs
arxiv-2602-19561.creator: Ryosuke Ikura 1 {}^{\textbf{1}}, Junya Hara 1 {}^{\textbf{1}} (Member, IEEE), Hiroshi Higashi 1 {}^{\textbf{1}} (Member, IEEE), and Yuichi Tanaka 1 {}^{\textbf{1}} (Senior Member, IEEE)
arxiv-2602-19561.description: Abstract This paper proposes a dynamic sensor scheduling method for sensor networks. In sensor network applications, we often need multiple equally-informative node subsets that are activated sequentially to make a sensor network robust against concentrated battery consumption and sensor failures. In addition, quality of these subsets changes dynamically and thus we must adapt those changes.

plos-pone-0008963.title: Impact of Herbivore Identity on Algal Succession and Coral Growth on a Caribbean Reef
plos-pone-0008963.creator: Deron E. Burkepile, Mark E. Hay
plos-pone-0008963.description: PLOS ONE research article. Herbivory is an important top-down force on coral reefs that regulates macroalgal abundance, mediates competitive interactions between macroalgae and corals, and provides resilience following disturbances such as hurricanes and coral bleaching. However, reductions in herbivore di

pmc-10527299.title: Mind the Gap: Model-Based Switching from Selatogrel to Maintenance Therapy with Oral P2Y12 Receptor Antagonists
pmc-10527299.creator: Chih-hsuan Hsin, Jasper Dingemanse, Andrea Henrich, Corine Bernaud, Martine Gehin, Andreas Krause
pmc-10527299.description: Background: The P2Y12 receptor antagonist selatogrel is being developed for subcutaneous self-administration with a ready-to-use autoinjector at the onset of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) symptoms. The unique pharmacological profile of selatogrel (fast, potent, and short-acting) can bridge the time gap between the onset of AMI and first medical care.

pmc-10691105.title: Pest recognition based on multi-image feature localization and adaptive filtering fusion
pmc-10691105.creator: Yanan Chen, Miao Chen, Minghui Guo, Jianji Wang, Nanning Zheng
pmc-10691105.description: Accurate recognition of pest categories is crucial for effective pest control. Due to issues such as the large variation in pest appearance, low data quality, and complex real-world environments, pest recognition poses challenges in practical applications. At present, many models have made great efforts on the real scene dataset IP102, but the highest recognition accuracy is only 75%.

pmc-10715245.title: Microbiome Alteration in Lung Tissues of Tuberculosis Patients Revealed by Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing and Immune-Related Transcriptional Profile Identified by Transcriptome Sequencing
pmc-10715245.creator: Hong Liu, Saiguang Ji, Yuan Fang, Xiaoli Yi, Fengsheng Wu, Fuchen Xing, Chenyan Wang, Hai Zhou, Jian Xu, Wei Sun
pmc-10715245.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This study explored alterations in the respiratory microbiome and transcriptome after Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection in tuberculosis (TB) patients. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) was adopted to reveal the microbiome in lung tissues from 110 TB and 25 nontuberculous (NonTB) patients. Transcriptome sequencing was performed in TB tissues (n = 3), tissues adjacent to TB (ParaTB, n = 3), and NonTB tissues (n = 3) to analyze differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and functional pathways.

pmc-13058640.title: Alarm bells or echoes of hope? A new perspective on the global youth mental health crisis
pmc-13058640.creator: Levi van Dam, Jim van Os, Geert Jan Stams, Hans Ormel
pmc-13058640.description: The youth mental health debate is often framed in alarming terms, yet evidence for a recent surge in mental disorder prevalence remains inconclusive. We argue that much of the apparent increase relies on self-report data, and thus may reflect heightened awareness of mental problems in youth themselves.

pmc-13103760.title: Graphene Dot–ZnO Hybrid Nanostructures as High-Performance Chemiresistive Sensors for H2S Detection
pmc-13103760.creator: Federica Bucolo, Daniela Iannazzo, Nesrine Hafiene, Consuelo Celesti, Roberto Di Pietro, Ulderico Wanderlingh, Sebastiano Vasi, Giovanni Neri
pmc-13103760.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The development of sensitive, selective, and low-cost gas sensors for hazardous pollutants remains a crucial challenge in environmental monitoring. Among gaseous pollutants, hydrogen sulfide (H2S) has been shown to negatively influence ecosystem dynamics. The novelty of this study lies in the synergistic integration of graphene dots (GDs) with ZnO, which significantly enhances the sensing performance while enabling efficient operation at a reduced temperature.

pmc-13284823.title: Pontine Hemorrhage Mimicking Bell’s Palsy: Isolated Facial Nerve Palsy—A Case Report
pmc-13284823.creator: Rei Takeichi, Nobukazu Miyamoto, Haruka Takeshige-Amano, Wataru Sako, Nobutaka Hattori

pmc-13372704.title: Machine learning-assisted prognosis prediction and surgical decision-making for glioblastoma: perceived benefits and concerns of patients, caregivers, and neurosurgeons
pmc-13372704.creator: Meredith V. Parsons, Olivia Buckley, Hamasa Ebadi, Eric Leuthardt, Tristan McIntosh
pmc-13372704.description: IntroductionIt is becoming more common for machine learning (ML) models to aid prognostication and clinical decision-making, including for glioblastoma (GBM) cases. However, there is a lack of empirical research on how end-users view potential benefits and risks of implementing such models in clinical practice.

pmc-13392218.title: From Diagnosis to Disclosure: Navigating Genetic Counseling Dilemmas in BRCA2‐Associated Prostate Cancer in the Middle East
pmc-13392218.creator: Chantel van Wyk, Reem Abdulrahim, Ilse Crous, Abeer Al Saegh, Amira Al Balushi, Bushra Al Muhairi, Sara Al Kiyumi, Suad Al Malki, Munjid Al Harthy, Neetu Rawal
pmc-13392218.description: BackgroundGermline genetic testing is integral to precision oncology in prostate cancer (PCa), particularly for men with pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) BRCA1/2 variants, where results have therapeutic and hereditary implications. However, data from the Middle East remain limited regarding real‐world implementation of genetic counseling and its influence on family communication and cascade testing.

pmc-13399332.title: Transparent, solvent‐free, and pressure‐tolerant antifouling coatings via molecular nanocomposite engineering
pmc-13399332.creator: Jieran Li, Xiubin Xu, Yueyan Liang, Hongchun Mu, Yang Xue, Jianwei Liu, Daijiang Cai, Yue Lan, Jiahui Tang, Sizhe Wang, Zhenxuan Wei, Xu Wu
pmc-13399332.description: Traditional solvent‐based antifouling coatings face critical limitations including application onto miscible organic substrates and volatile organic compound (VOCs) pollution. Herein, this work presented a solvent‐free, transparent antifouling coating through room temperature vulcanization, based on a strategy of molecularly engineered nanocomposite networks.
